name: scummvm-tools
why: A toolkit for extracting and converting resources from classic adventure game data files, a good door into old game formats.

brief.what_it_is: scummvm-tools is a collection of utilities that work with ScummVM and the original data files of classic adventure games. The extraction and compression tools can run from the command line or from a GUI wizard, and the rest are command-line only. Inputs are original game data files, such as archives, disk images, and scripts. Outputs are extracted resources, recompressed audio (MP3, Vorbis, or FLAC), rebuilt data packs, or decompiled and disassembled scripts. The main entry point is scummvm-tools-cli, which auto-detects the right tool from the input file. The package installs about 44 executables, but the README documents only some of them; names such as grim_*, saga_unpack, and msn_convert_mod are not described there.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the tools are 'a collection of various tools that may be useful to use in conjunction with ScummVM.' They help people turn original game files into formats ScummVM can read, and let them inspect or convert the game scripts.
brief.how_it_works: scummvm-tools-cli takes an input file, detects which tool to use, and writes output by default to an out/ directory next to the input. Extraction and compression are selected with the extract or compress modes, or by naming a tool with --tool. Audio format flags (--mp3, --flac, --vorbis) and tool-specific options are passed before the input file. The script tools, such as decine, degob, and descumm, are standalone decompilers or disassemblers that take a script file and a version or type flag.

commands_seen.context: General syntax from the README. Auto-detects the tool from the input file; extract or compress is a hint.
Runs a named tool directly instead of relying on auto-detection.
Extracts packed files from the Amiga and AtariST versions of Elvira 1/2, Waxworks and Simon the Sorcerer 1.
Unpacks Kyrandia .PAK files; -x extracts all files from the Hand of Fate installer package.
Extracts data files from the Commodore 64 version of Maniac Mansion.
Compresses Simon the Sorcerer voc/wav files to Vorbis at quality 7.
Example of compress_scumm_sou with the MP3 flag, producing a .so3 file.
Compresses Broken Sword 2 music and speech .clu files to .cl3, .clg, or .clf.
Decompiles Delphine Cinematique scripts. Type is -prc or -rel; version is -v1 (Future Wars) or -v2 (Operation Stealth).
Decompiles TOT scripts from Coktel Vision games. Version names include Gob1, Gob2, Gob3, Woodruff, and others.

brief.install_notes: The README gives no Homebrew-specific steps. Extraction usually needs the original game data files, and some tools need particular inputs such as Maniac Mansion disk images or a Loom CD dump. The shell scripts need external programs: extract_loom_tg16.sh uses cdrdao, bchunk, and optionally flac, and convert_dxa.sh uses FFmpeg. The Loom TG16 extraction also needs a CD dump, described on the wiki. Run scummvm-tools-cli --help <tool name> for each tool's options.
brief.standout: One binary covers many unrelated games, from Sierra and LucasArts to Coktel Vision, Westwood, and Delphine, and can auto-detect the tool for a given file. It is also a practical way to see how the games stored their data before ScummVM played them.
brief.status: unknown for the tools module. The README's 'Last updated' line still reads the unexpanded SVN keyword '$Date$', and it gives no release date. The main ScummVM site is very active, with release 2026.4.0 announced in October 2026, but that does not show whether this tools repository is still being maintained.
brief.caveats: The README warns that the tools are 'not always in-sync with the latest STABLE version of ScummVM', so a tool's output may not match the ScummVM version you run. Some compression output needs a ScummVM build with zlib, Ogg, or MP3 support. Some tools have version gaps: compress_gob's output is for Gobliiins, compress_sci does not handle SCI32 games, compress_sword1 does not handle the PSX version, and extract_mm_nes does not handle the Japanese version. The GUI wizard is only for extraction and compression. The homepage fetch returned ScummVM's main site, not material about these tools.
quotes: This is a collection of various tools that may be useful to use in conjunction with ScummVM.
The extraction and compression tools can either be run from the command line or using the GUI wizard. All other tools are only available in command line.
Please note that this module is not always in-sync with the latest STABLE version of ScummVM.

https://github.com/scummvm/scummvm-tools - worked, returned the README, which contains the tool documentation used for this brief

judge.reason: It opens up the internals of classic games, from extracting obscure disk formats to decompiling their scripts, making it more than a routine archive utility.

entry.title: scummvm-tools
entry.tldr: About 44 utilities that unpack, convert and decompile the data files of classic adventure games, a hands-on way into how old games stored their assets.
entry.deeper_look:
scummvm-tools is a companion kit for ScummVM, the engine that replays old adventure games. It takes original game files such as archives, disk images and compiled scripts, and turns them into something readable. Outputs include extracted resources, recompressed audio (MP3, Vorbis or FLAC), rebuilt data packs, and decompiled or disassembled scripts.

The main entry point is `scummvm-tools-cli`. Give it an input file and it works out which tool to use, writing results to an `out/` directory next to the input. You can also name a tool with `--tool`. The extraction and compression tools also have a GUI wizard. The rest, including script decompilers such as `descumm`, `decine` and `degob`, are command-line only.

The idea underneath is that every game studio invented its own way of packing data. Sierra, LucasArts, Coktel Vision, Westwood and Delphine each did it differently. Each tool here encodes what someone learned about one of those formats, so reading what a tool does is a short course in file-format archaeology. The README describes the set as "a collection of various tools that may be useful to use in conjunction with ScummVM." It documents only some of the executables. Names like `grim_*`, `saga_unpack` and `msn_convert_mod` are not described there.
entry.install:
brew install scummvm-tools
# Most tools need original game data files, which you must supply yourself.
# Some shell scripts need extras: cdrdao and bchunk (Loom TG16), FFmpeg (convert_dxa.sh).

try_this.what_happens: Prints the supported tools, which shows how many different games and formats the kit covers.
Shows general usage. The brief says `--help <tool name>` gives each tool's options.
Shows usage for the Delphine Cinematique script decompiler, which takes a type (-prc or -rel) and a version (-v1 for Future Wars, -v2 for Operation Stealth).

entry.whats_unique: One command-line front end covers many unrelated games and picks the right tool from the input file. Few projects put this many old adventure-game formats in one place.
entry.caveats: The README warns the tools are "not always in-sync with the latest STABLE version of ScummVM", its maintenance status is unclear, and almost everything needs original game files you must already own.
